ranked_facts.why: The presence of a milky white layer on the surface of the blood sample, indicative of hypertriglyceridemia, is more characteristic of lipoprotein lipase deficiency, a type of lipid storage disease, than glycogen storage disease, and does not strongly support or contrast with lysosomal storage disease, congenital disorder of glycosylation, or other metabolic disorders.

Hypertriglyceridemia causing lactescent plasma is a hallmark of lipoprotein lipase deficiency, which is a lipid storage disease, and is less commonly associated with glycogen storage disease, and does not strongly support or contrast with lysosomal storage disease, congenital disorder of glycosylation, or other metabolic disorders.
